items.message: read_catalog allows local filesystem reads when the URL does not start with 'http', gated only by `root is not None`. A Source registered via market.toml with a relative or absolute path URL bypasses check_url entirely, since add_source enforces https but sources() reads market.toml without re-validating URLs. An attacker who can write or influence .lockstep/market.toml (e.g., via a malicious PR or a compromised dependency that writes to the repo) can set url = "/etc/passwd" or url = "../../../s…[truncated]

fetch reads the response with response.read(MAX_INDEX_BYTES + 1) and then checks length, but the full over-limit read has already occurred in memory before the check fires. For a 1 MB limit this is a bounded issue (1 MB + 1 byte held), but the pattern means the size check does not bound peak allocation — it only detects the violation after the fact.

add_source writes name and url directly into the TOML output via an f-string without escaping: `f'[source."{key}"]
url = "{value}"

'`. A name or URL containing a double-quote or newline can break out of the quoted TOML value and inject arbitrary TOML structure into market.toml.
